use maintained protocol library; validate signature, allowed algorithms, issuer, audience, expiry and intended token type; reject untrusted keys
token revocation gap - a revoked session or credential remains valid beyond policy
define revocation latency, short lifetimes and appropriate introspection or revocation state; avoid assuming self-contained tokens revoke instantly
oauth and oidc binding failure - a callback, authorization code or identity assertion is accepted for the wrong client or session
use authorization code flow with pkce where applicable, exact redirect allowlist, session-bound state and oidc nonce validation; use standard library
account enumeration - authentication or recovery reveals whether an account exists
use consistent outward responses, bounded attempts and asynchronous recovery where appropriate; avoid leaking account status
unsafe account recovery - recovery credentials allow unauthorized resets or repeat use
use high-entropy purpose-bound single-use tokens stored safely, atomic redemption, short expiry and post-reset session policy
workload identity impersonation - a service accepts a spoofed workload identity or credentials from the wrong environment
use authenticated workload identities, short-lived credentials and explicit audience/environment trust; authorize each operation
security extension 2
authorization and business-flow security
object-level authorization failure - a valid caller accesses another principal's resource by identifier
enforce ownership or explicit grants at the protected data operation; derive tenant from trusted context
function-level authorization failure - a caller reaches privileged functions without required rights
deny by default; enforce permissions server-side at each privileged function and validate delegated authority
unsafe property binding - client-controlled fields alter protected attributes such as roles or owner ids
allowlist writable properties by operation and policy; map explicit request types and derive server-owned fields
unauthorized property disclosure - an authorized object response exposes fields the caller cannot see
apply field-level read authorization and explicit projections; omit sensitive fields before serialization
fail-open authorization - policy errors or unavailable identity services permit access
fail closed on protected operations when authority is uncertain; define separate public or degraded behavior
privilege administration abuse - permission changes allow unauthorized escalation or bypass separation of duties
authorize grant creation and scope; enforce privilege ceilings and approval for high-impact grants; audit changes
sensitive business-flow abuse - valid automated actions exhaust limited business resources or circumvent policy
enforce business-specific quotas, state constraints and risk controls at authoritative boundary; avoid only ip limits
unsafe cross-origin trust - browser credentials or protected responses are exposed to untrusted origins
allow only required origins, methods and headers; use explicit credential policy and keep server-side authorization
security extension 3
injection and untrusted content
sql injection - untrusted values alter database query semantics
bind parameters for values and allowlist identifiers; avoid constructing sql from untrusted strings
nosql query injection - untrusted structures become database operators or filters
validate typed inputs, construct filters server-side and allowlist permitted operators
command injection - untrusted values alter operating-system command execution
avoid shell execution; use constrained direct apis and validated arguments, with least privilege
cross-site scripting - untrusted content is interpreted as active browser code
use context-aware output encoding and vetted sanitization for intended html; csp is defense in depth
server-side request forgery - untrusted destinations cause server requests across restricted network boundaries
use approved destinations or isolated fetch service, enforce address policy after resolution and redirects, bound response size/time
cross-site request forgery - a browser sends an authenticated state change without user intent
use anti-forgery controls appropriate to credential mode, origin validation and safe http semantics; do not rely solely on cors
unsafe xml processing - xml parsing resolves external resources or expands input unexpectedly
disable unneeded external entities and dtds; use safe parser configuration and resource limits
unsafe deserialization - untrusted serialized data constructs unexpected objects or executes behavior
use data-only serialization and explicit schema/type allowlists; verify integrity when appropriate
path traversal and archive extraction - untrusted paths escape authorized directories or overwrite unrelated files
use trusted roots, safe path resolution and symlink-aware filesystem primitives; reject unsafe archive entries
template injection - untrusted content is interpreted as template source
use trusted templates with data-only bindings; sandbox only as additional control
unsafe redirect - untrusted destination redirects users outside intended trust boundary
use local paths or explicit trusted destinations; normalize and validate before redirecting
http parser disagreement - intermediaries disagree on request boundaries or normalization
reject ambiguous framing at ingress, align parser behavior and patch intermediaries
unsafe file upload - untrusted files become executable, public or resource-exhausting content
allowlist business-required types, verify content, enforce limits, store outside executable paths and quarantine when needed
unsafe upstream api consumption - third-party responses bypass validation or inject unsafe data into local actions
validate external data against explicit contracts, bound resources and enforce local authorization before effects
security extension 4
data protection and cryptography
hardcoded secrets - reusable credentials are embedded in code, images or defaults
use secret manager or injected scoped credentials; revoke exposed secrets and remove insecure defaults
secret exposure in artifacts and history - credentials persist in repository history, package or build output
revoke and rotate first; remove exposure from artifacts/history with coordinated owner approval; prevent recurrence
unprotected sensitive storage - sensitive data or snapshots are readable outside intended access boundary
apply appropriate encryption and restricted access, separate key authority and minimize retained data
cleartext sensitive transport - sensitive data or credentials traverse untrusted links without protection
use authenticated encryption in transit for relevant trust boundaries; enforce transport policy and secure downgrade handling
disabled tls certificate validation - a client trusts an unauthenticated endpoint
validate certificate chain and hostname with approved trust anchors; provision internal ca rather than disabling checks
weak password storage - password records can be recovered cheaply after a breach
use maintained password hashing with suitable cost and unique salts; migrate legacy hashes safely
unsafe cryptographic primitive or mode - encryption or signatures do not provide the required security property
use approved authenticated encryption/signature protocols and reviewed libraries; avoid custom cryptography
cryptographic nonce reuse - a key is used with repeated nonces where uniqueness is required
use library-supported nonce policy appropriate to algorithm; ensure uniqueness per key across replicas and recovery
predictable security tokens - security-sensitive identifiers derive from predictable randomness
use cryptographically secure randomness of appropriate entropy; do not use timestamps or ordinary prng for secrets
key lifecycle and rotation failure - expired or compromised keys remain trusted, or rotation breaks availability
use versioned keys, bounded overlap, rotation and revocation procedures; protect historical decrypt needs separately
sensitive data lifecycle mismatch - data survives beyond deletion or retention policy in copies or derived stores
minimize copies, enforce retention and deletion propagation subject to documented legal holds and restore controls
security extension 5
distributed and infrastructure security
unauthenticated internal service - an internal endpoint trusts network location instead of identity
authenticate and authorize service calls at the protected boundary; use network controls as defense in depth
unrestricted network reachability - a compromised workload can reach unrelated sensitive services
allow required flows explicitly, separate trust zones and verify policy enforcement by runtime/network provider
unauthorized message operations - a client can publish, consume or administer unrelated queues or topics
separate producer/consumer identities and scope permissions to required destinations and operations
message integrity and trust failure - a service accepts unauthenticated or altered messages as authoritative
authenticate transport and publisher where required; validate envelope, schema and authorization; sign payloads when end-to-end integrity needed
excessive workload privileges - runtime permissions exceed application needs, enabling unintended access
use least privilege, non-root where feasible, minimal capabilities and restricted mounts; document justified exceptions
exposed management surface - administrative or debug endpoints are reachable by unintended clients
restrict network and identity access, disable unnecessary endpoints, separate administration plane
insecure deployment defaults - unsafe defaults remain enabled in deployed environments
define secure baseline, validate on startup or admission and prevent unsafe production defaults
cross-environment credential reuse - development or staging credentials grant production access
separate accounts, trust roots and credential scopes by environment; restrict promotion workflows
stale api inventory - deprecated or shadow endpoints escape security policy and patching
maintain versioned inventory and retirement controls; apply security policy consistently to all reachable versions
security extension 6
software supply chain
vulnerable dependency exposure - a known vulnerable dependency is reachable in application or deployment
use authorized sca, update or mitigate affected versions, document exceptions and retest compatibility
dependency confusion - a resolver retrieves an unintended package from an untrusted namespace or registry
pin trusted registries and namespaces; lock dependency resolution and verify package integrity
artifact integrity failure - deployment accepts modified or unverified binaries/images
verify signatures or attestations against trusted identities, pin immutable digests and enforce policy at promotion
untrusted ci execution - untrusted contributions can execute with privileged pipeline context
separate untrusted builds from privileged release jobs, use minimal token permissions and approved promotion
pipeline credential leakage - build credentials are exposed in logs, caches, artifacts or long-lived tokens
prefer short-lived workload identity, isolated credentials, redaction and restricted artifact access
missing build provenance - an artifact cannot be traced to approved source and build process
generate and verify provenance and dependency inventory at controlled build/promotion; keep trust policy independent
unsupported component lifecycle - runtime or dependency no longer receives required security fixes
maintain lifecycle inventory, upgrade path and time-bounded risk acceptance for unsupported components
security extension 7
security monitoring and operations
missing security audit coverage - security-relevant actions cannot be attributed or investigated
record actor, action, target, outcome and correlation with minimal sensitive data; durable audit intent where required
audit trail tampering - unauthorized actors can alter or remove security evidence
separate audit authority, restrict deletion, use append-only or tamper-evident controls appropriate to risk
security alerting gap - abuse or control failure does not trigger actionable notification
define monitored security signals, thresholds, escalation and test alert delivery; avoid noisy alerts without ownership
error information disclosure - failures reveal internal implementation or sensitive values to callers
return sanitized error contracts, maintain restricted diagnostics and correlation; never expose secret or stack details publicly
security configuration drift - effective controls diverge from approved baseline unnoticed
continuously validate effective controls, review changes and alert on unauthorized deviations
emergency credential response gap - compromised credentials cannot be revoked or isolated within required time
define emergency rotation/revocation and containment with tested dependencies and communication; preserve service recovery
security extension 8
ai and agentic application security
prompt injection trust-boundary failure - untrusted user or retrieved content influences privileged agent behavior
treat content as data; enforce independent tool authorization, constrained actions and output validation outside model; no prompt-only guarantee
excessive agent authority - agent credentials or tools exceed the requested task scope
use scoped tools, least privilege, explicit authorization and confirmation for high-impact actions; enforce in host
rag authorization bypass - retrieval returns documents the caller cannot access
enforce document-level authorization at retrieval and revalidate access where needed; scope indexes/caches by policy
agent memory isolation failure - persistent memory leaks data or instructions across tenant or task boundaries
scope memory to authorized identity/tenant and purpose, validate provenance and support deletion; avoid treating memory as trusted authority
knowledge and model input poisoning - untrusted ingestion corrupts knowledge or model inputs used for decisions
validate source and content, track provenance, quarantine untrusted updates and provide version rollback
unsafe model output execution - generated text becomes executable commands, code or privileged data without validation
treat outputs as untrusted data, schema-validate, use constrained apis and sandbox approved execution; require authority separately
unbounded agent execution and cost - agent loops or tool fan-out exhaust budgets or trigger repeated effects
enforce host-level budgets, cancellation, concurrency limits and idempotent effects; stop safely and report incomplete work
untrusted tool or mcp integration - a tool definition or result expands authority or sends data to unintended party
allowlist trusted servers/tools, verify identity and contracts, constrain egress and permissions; treat descriptions/results as untrusted
ai sensitive output disclosure - model responses reveal sensitive information from context, tools or memory
minimize sensitive inputs, enforce retrieval permissions, validate output and apply provider/data retention policy; never rely only on filtering
agent-to-agent trust failure - peer messages are accepted as authoritative instructions without verified identity or delegation
authenticate peers, validate delegated scope and message schema, and independently authorize requested effects

signals are investigation leads, not findings
confirm the business invariant and actual runtime guarantees
tests are proposals until executed in an isolated environment
use the simplest sufficient safeguard; do not introduce a pattern merely because it is listed
sdp-069 - duplicate api submission
failure: users submit the same request multiple times
detection: repeated post creates multiple records
remediation and safeguards: scoped idempotency or durable business uniqueness; request fingerprint
verification: repeat and concurrently submit same operation; one record/effect
decision: confirm reachability, existing constraints and the required guarantee before reporting a defect; document any remaining uncertainty
sdp-070 - timeout ambiguity
failure: a client cannot determine whether a timed-out operation completed
detection: timeout interpreted as failure and new operation created
remediation and safeguards: return stable operation id and status endpoint; reconcile uncertain result
verification: drop response after commit; query resolves original result
sdp-071 - long-running request
failure: operations exceed http or gateway timeout limits
detection: http request holds resources through long job
remediation and safeguards: durable enqueue and 202/status contract; idempotent submit and worker
verification: disconnect client and restart api; job completes or reports durable failure
sdp-072 - concurrent api updates
failure: multiple clients overwrite the same resource
detection: put/patch ignores resource version
remediation and safeguards: etag/if-match or equivalent compare-and-swap; surface conflict
verification: two clients edit same version; second gets conflict instead of silent overwrite
sdp-073 - api request flooding
failure: excessive requests overwhelm backend services
detection: no bounded request admission or per-identity quotas
remediation and safeguards: rate and concurrency limits at relevant scope; explicit retry guidance
verification: burst per identity and across identities; capacity and fairness maintained
sdp-074 - n+1 request problem
failure: retrieving a collection generates an additional request for every item
detection: loop issues one query/rpc per item
remediation and safeguards: batch or eager load with bounded page size; inspect query counts
verification: increase item count; calls scale by batches not individual items
sdp-075 - overfetching
failure: apis return unnecessary data
detection: endpoint returns unused or sensitive fields by default
remediation and safeguards: projection and explicit authorized response contract
verification: compare payload size and fields for representative clients; no restricted fields
sdp-076 - underfetching
failure: clients require multiple api calls to retrieve related information
detection: client must issue many sequential dependent requests
remediation and safeguards: compose or batch required data with bounded fan-out
verification: measure network calls and latency; failure semantics remain explicit
sdp-077 - pagination drift
failure: records are skipped or duplicated when data changes between page requests
detection: offset pages shift under concurrent insert/delete
remediation and safeguards: stable unique ordering and keyset cursor; snapshot if complete enumeration required
verification: insert/delete between pages; no unintended duplicates or omissions under contract
sdp-078 - request replay attack
failure: previously valid requests are maliciously resubmitted
detection: signed or authenticated action can be replayed
remediation and safeguards: bind signature to method/body/context; enforce nonce/window and durable uniqueness where needed
verification: replay valid request within and outside window; unauthorized repeat rejected
sdp-079 - partial bulk operation failure
failure: some items succeed while others fail
detection: batch retries repeat successful items or hides partial results
remediation and safeguards: item-level durable identities and status; explicit atomic or partial contract
verification: fail midway then retry batch; successful items not repeated
sdp-080 - api fan-out failure
failure: an aggregated response fails because one dependency is unavailable
detection: parallel aggregation fails whole response on optional dependency
remediation and safeguards: classify required/optional dependencies; bound fan-out and return explicit partial state
verification: fail optional and mandatory dependencies separately; contract matches policy
references/problems-caching.md: caching - problem playbook
sdp-011 - stale data
failure: cache contains an outdated version of database records
detection: ttl exceeds freshness requirement or critical decisions use cached state
remediation and safeguards: specify freshness; invalidate after commit; authoritative recheck for critical decisions
verification: update source and measure visibility bound; stale display never authorizes invalid write
sdp-012 - dual write problem
failure: database update succeeds, but cache update fails, or vice versa
detection: cache and db writes independently succeed
remediation and safeguards: commit db first; durable invalidation intent if required; versioned cache protocol
verification: fail cache call after db commit; eventual invalidation within declared bound
sdp-013 - cache stampede (thundering herd)
failure: multiple requests simultaneously regenerate an expired cache entry
detection: every miss independently loads same expensive key
remediation and safeguards: coalesce by scoped key; bound waiters and fallback; coordinate across replicas if needed
verification: expire hot key under parallel load; measure bounded source fetches
sdp-014 - cache avalanche
failure: large numbers of cached records expire simultaneously
detection: bulk population sets identical expiry timestamps
remediation and safeguards: jitter expiry and refresh gradually while respecting maximum staleness
verification: expire representative key population; source load stays within capacity
sdp-015 - cache penetration
failure: requests for nonexistent records repeatedly reach the database
detection: repeated absent keys trigger expensive reads
remediation and safeguards: bound negative cache ttl and size; invalidate on create; rate limit adversarial misses
verification: flood absent keys then create one; load bounded and new record visible
sdp-016 - cache breakdown
failure: a frequently accessed cache key expires, overwhelming the database
detection: hot key refresh blocks or floods source
remediation and safeguards: singleflight and permitted stale serving with hard freshness bound
verification: expire busiest key with slow source; latency and load stay bounded
sdp-017 - hot key problem
failure: one cache key receives disproportionately high traffic
detection: one partition or cache key saturates server
remediation and safeguards: replicate immutable reads or use local cache with invalidation; avoid splitting authoritative counters unsafely
verification: skew load to one key; check throughput and freshness
sdp-018 - cache poisoning
failure: incorrect or malicious data is stored in the cache
detection: cache key omits representation or trusted authorization dimensions
remediation and safeguards: canonicalize key inputs; validate cacheable responses; isolate private data
verification: vary host/header/tenant inputs; unauthorized or corrupted response never reused
sdp-019 - cache invalidation race
failure: a concurrent request repopulates the cache with outdated data
detection: reader fetches old db version then writes after invalidation
remediation and safeguards: use generation/version comparison atomic at cache or coordinate reads/writes; retain invalidation watermark
verification: pause old reader until writer commits and invalidates; old value cannot repopulate past bound
sdp-020 - cold cache problem
failure: application startup generates excessive database requests
detection: all replicas start with empty caches and full traffic
remediation and safeguards: gradual admission, bounded warming, source capacity budget
verification: restart replicas together; database stays within connection and latency limits
sdp-021 - cache dependency failure
failure: cache outage causes database overload
detection: cache error falls back to unlimited database calls
remediation and safeguards: bound fallback concurrency; shed optional work; preserve authoritative correctness
verification: disable cache under load; db remains healthy and overload responses are controlled
sdp-022 - cache memory exhaustion
failure: cached data consumes all available memory
detection: unbounded keys or large values consume cache memory
remediation and safeguards: set capacity, eviction and item limits; separate durable coordination data from evictable cache
verification: generate high-cardinality keys; memory bounded and critical state preserved
references/problems-data-migration.md: data migration - problem playbook
sdp-105 - multi-writer conflict
failure: independent writers overwrite concurrent changes
detection: independent regions/services overwrite by wall-clock last writer
remediation and safeguards: single writer or domain-approved merge with causal/version tracking
verification: concurrent conflicting updates under partition; resolution meets invariant
sdp-106 - tombstone resurrection
failure: delayed replication or replay recreates a deleted entity
detection: deletion metadata removed before delayed updates expire
remediation and safeguards: versioned tombstones retained across replay horizon; reject older writes
verification: delete then replay old create; entity stays deleted
sdp-107 - projection rebuild inconsistency
failure: a rebuilt read model loses concurrent changes or exposes incomplete state
detection: projection rebuilt from snapshot without concurrent catch-up
remediation and safeguards: consistent snapshot/checkpoint, catch-up and atomic cutover
verification: write during rebuild; new projection matches authoritative state at cutover
sdp-108 - mixed-version deployment
failure: old and new instances cannot share schemas or contracts
detection: schema/contract change breaks old live instances
remediation and safeguards: expand-contract; test old/new readers and writers and rollback compatibility
verification: run mixed versions through migration; both operate until contract phase
sdp-109 - backfill race
failure: a migration backfill overwrites newer live writes
detection: backfill overwrites values changed after scan
remediation and safeguards: conditional versioned updates, resumable bounded batches
verification: pause backfill then update live row; backfill cannot overwrite newer value
sdp-110 - restore inconsistency
failure: restoring one store replays side effects or diverges from other stores
detection: stores restored to incompatible points or replay effects uncontrolled
remediation and safeguards: document recovery dependencies, aligned checkpoints and reconciliation; isolate replay effects
verification: restore disposable stores with skewed checkpoints; reconcile before reopening writes
sdp-111 - cdc retention gap
failure: a connector resumes after its source log position is no longer available
detection: cdc offset older than retained log
remediation and safeguards: monitor retention headroom; stop unsafe resume; controlled resnapshot with catch-up
verification: expire source offset; recovery detects gap and rebuilds without silent loss
references/problems-database.md: database - problem playbook
sdp-023 - dual write (database + message broker)
failure: database commits successfully, but the corresponding event is not published
detection: database commit and broker publish separate operations
remediation and safeguards: write outbox in same local transaction; relay with confirmations and idempotent consumer
verification: crash before publish and after broker confirm before mark; event eventually processed once in effect
sdp-024 - duplicate event processing
failure: the same event is delivered and processed multiple times
detection: consumer dedupe check separate from mutation
remediation and safeguards: unique inbox claim and business mutation in one transaction; external effects separately protected
verification: deliver identical event concurrently and after crash; one business mutation
sdp-025 - dirty read
failure: a transaction reads another transaction's uncommitted data
detection: read uncommitted or equivalent reads drive decisions
remediation and safeguards: use committed isolation or stronger as invariant requires; inspect engine settings
verification: hold uncommitted update then roll back; reader never acts on dirty value
sdp-026 - non-repeatable read
failure: reading the same record twice produces different values within one transaction
detection: repeated reads assume stable row under read committed
remediation and safeguards: use suitable repeatable snapshot or lock; check engine semantics
verification: update between reads; transaction observes required stable view or detects conflict
sdp-027 - phantom read
failure: new records appear between repeated queries within a transaction
detection: range count used for invariant without predicate protection
remediation and safeguards: serializable/predicate lock or materialized constraint; retry serialization failures
verification: concurrent inserts into checked range; invariant survives
sdp-028 - write skew
failure: concurrent transactions independently satisfy conditions but collectively violate a business rule
detection: disjoint writes depend on shared snapshot predicate
remediation and safeguards: serializable isolation or lock shared invariant row; verify actual engine behavior
verification: two transactions independently pass predicate; at least one aborts if combined invalid
sdp-029 - database deadlock
failure: transactions wait on each other's locks until interrupted
detection: opposite lock acquisition order or long transactions
remediation and safeguards: order locks consistently; shorten transaction; retry whole safe transaction after deadlock
verification: force opposing lock order; bounded recovery without duplicate external effects
sdp-030 - race condition
failure: the result depends on the execution order of concurrent operations
detection: shared mutable state or check-then-act across threads/processes
remediation and safeguards: use authoritative atomic operation or correctly scoped synchronization
verification: force competing interleaving; invariant holds across processes
sdp-031 - replication lag
failure: a read replica returns outdated data after a successful write
detection: post-write read routed to lagging replica
remediation and safeguards: route consistency-sensitive read to primary or wait for commit watermark
verification: delay replica apply; caller sees own write or explicit pending state
sdp-032 - split-brain
failure: multiple database nodes incorrectly believe they are the primary
detection: two primaries accept writes after partition
remediation and safeguards: quorum-backed leadership and fencing at storage; define minority behavior
verification: partition old primary then promote new; stale primary cannot commit
sdp-033 - database hotspot
failure: excessive transactions target a specific record or partition
detection: single row/partition serialized under skewed workload
remediation and safeguards: measure contention; partition only if invariants allow; batch or redesign allocation
verification: skew traffic and inspect lock waits; correctness unchanged at target load
sdp-034 - cross-database transaction
failure: a business transaction spans multiple independent databases
detection: independent db commits assumed atomic
remediation and safeguards: prefer one ownership boundary; otherwise saga/tcc or justified supported 2pc with recovery
verification: crash between database commits; recover to defined valid state
sdp-035 - database connection exhaustion
failure: requests consume all available database connections
detection: connections held across remote calls or unbounded pool per replica
remediation and safeguards: shorten scope; cap total pools and admission; dispose on error
verification: saturate dependency and scale replicas; connection count bounded and recovery occurs
sdp-036 - inconsistent distributed data
failure: independent services maintain conflicting versions of business data
detection: multiple services mutate same logical field without authority
remediation and safeguards: assign owner; version events and reconcile derived copies
verification: apply delayed conflicting update; owner wins by defined policy
sdp-037 - orphaned records
failure: related records remain after incomplete operations or deletions
detection: child created without valid parent or deletion leaves dangling references
remediation and safeguards: foreign keys where local; durable lifecycle and reconciliation across boundaries
verification: fail parent/child lifecycle halfway; no invalid live child remains
references/problems-deployment-resources: deployment resources - problem playbook
sdp-137 - configuration drift
failure: replicas use incompatible safety settings
detection: replica configuration differs on consistency-critical settings
remediation and safeguards: version config and validate invariants on startup; compare live configuration safely
verification: start mismatched replicas; invalid config rejected or explicitly quarantined
sdp-138 - incompatible rollback
failure: old application cannot handle migrated data
detection: rollback deploys old binary after irreversible schema/data change
remediation and safeguards: maintain compatibility window or forward-fix plan; verify rollback preconditions
verification: apply migration then run supported rollback; no corrupt reads/writes
sdp-139 - migration lock contention
failure: ddl blocks live workload
detection: ddl holds blocking lock during normal traffic
remediation and safeguards: plan engine-specific online operations or controlled downtime; bound lock waits
verification: run migration with representative concurrent traffic; lock impact within budget
sdp-140 - concurrent migration execution
failure: multiple replicas apply schema changes concurrently
detection: every replica runs migration independently at startup
remediation and safeguards: single coordinated migration owner and versioned history; enforce safe startup
verification: start replicas simultaneously; migration executes safely once in effect
sdp-141 - thread pool starvation
failure: blocking work exhausts execution threads
detection: blocking i/o or sync waits exhaust request execution threads
remediation and safeguards: use asynchronous i/o where appropriate; bound blocking pools and work
verification: slow i/o under concurrency; thread use bounded and healthy requests progress
sdp-142 - resource handle leak
failure: failure paths retain connections or streams
detection: connections/streams not disposed on exceptions or cancellation
remediation and safeguards: structured cleanup and bounded lifetimes; monitor open handles
verification: repeat failed/canceled operations; handle counts return to baseline
sdp-143 - unbounded memory growth
failure: accumulated state or tasks exhaust memory
detection: unbounded collection or in-flight tasks grow under sustained load
remediation and safeguards: bound queues, caches and retained results; apply backpressure and eviction
verification: run sustained load; memory stabilizes and overload handled
sdp-144 - autoscaling feedback mismatch
failure: scaling signal ignores actual bottleneck
detection: autoscaler reacts to cpu while queue age or dependency saturation dominates
remediation and safeguards: use workload-appropriate signals and downstream capacity caps; stabilize scaling
verification: burst queue workload with low cpu; scale safely and drain backlog
sdp-145 - cancellation resource leak
failure: canceled requests leave expensive work running
detection: timeout cancels caller but expensive work continues consuming capacity
remediation and safeguards: propagate cooperative cancellation; isolate bounded noncancelable tasks; track actual completion
verification: cancel many slow operations; active resources return within declared bound

sdp-101 - monetary rounding drift
failure: binary floating point or inconsistent rounding changes financial totals
detection: binary float used for money or inconsistent rounding boundaries
remediation and safeguards: use exact decimal/minor units; explicit rounding and allocation residual rules
verification: split amount across items and recombine; totals equal approved amount
sdp-102 - currency mixing
failure: ledger entries or balances mix incompatible currencies
detection: amounts summed without currency dimension
remediation and safeguards: currency-aware types and per-currency posting; explicit fx legs and rates
verification: attempt mixed-currency sum/post; reject or convert by authorized rule
sdp-103 - idempotency retention gap
failure: a delayed retry arrives after its deduplication key expires
detection: dedupe ttl shorter than replay/retry horizon
remediation and safeguards: align retention or durable business uniqueness beyond ttl
verification: replay after expiry but within supported horizon; no duplicate effect
sdp-104 - concurrent idempotency claim
failure: two requests both see an unused key before processing
detection: non-atomic check then claim of operation key
remediation and safeguards: unique scoped atomic claim, payload hash and durable outcome; handle in-progress
verification: concurrent same-key requests and mismatched payload; one claim and mismatch rejected
references/problems-financial.md: financial - problem playbook
sdp-001 - duplicate charge
failure: a customer is charged multiple times due to retries or network failures
detection: charge called before durable operation claim; retry uses new provider key
remediation and safeguards: persist unique scoped operation and request hash; reuse provider key; reconcile unknown outcomes
verification: lose provider response after charge and retry concurrently; assert one provider charge and one ledger effect
sdp-002 - inconsistent financial balance
failure: money is deducted from one account without being credited to another
detection: debit and credit committed separately or unbalanced journal allowed
remediation and safeguards: post balanced entries atomically per currency; enforce posting invariant and reversal semantics
verification: crash between legs; assert neither posts or both post and journal balances
sdp-003 - double spending
failure: the same available balance is spent through concurrent transactions
detection: balance read then unconditional debit
remediation and safeguards: conditional debit or serializable locked invariant check in same transaction
verification: two spends exceeding combined balance; only admissible spend commits
sdp-004 - lost update
failure: two transactions update the same record, overwriting each other's changes
detection: read-modify-write without version predicate
remediation and safeguards: compare version on update; reject conflict or recompute safely
verification: two readers update same version; no silent overwrite
sdp-005 - partial transaction failure
failure: some operations succeed while others fail
detection: multiple durable effects with no recovery state
remediation and safeguards: use local transaction if possible; otherwise durable saga with idempotent compensation
verification: fail each step after prior commit; recover or compensate to valid state
sdp-006 - uncertain transaction status
failure: a payment succeeds, but the client receives a timeout
detection: timeout mapped to definitive payment failure
remediation and safeguards: persist unknown outcome and query provider by stable reference before retry
verification: drop successful provider response; reconcile without second payment
sdp-007 - financial record manipulation
failure: historical financial transactions are modified or deleted
detection: posted journal editable via ordinary crud
remediation and safeguards: restrict updates and deletes; append reversal with actor and reason; audit privileged access
verification: attempt edit/delete via api and db role; reversal preserves history
sdp-008 - balance calculation drift
failure: stored balances become inconsistent with transaction history
detection: stored balance independently changed from journal
remediation and safeguards: derive or atomically maintain projection; compare ledger totals and repair conditionally
verification: inject projection drift; reconciliation detects and repairs without changing journal
sdp-009 - concurrent resource reservation
failure: multiple users reserve the same seat, room or inventory item
detection: availability check separated from reservation write
